notes: The claim accurately reflects that in isolated MR total LV stroke volume includes forward and backward flow, reduced afterload maintains ejection fraction until advanced disease, and parameters like LVEF and GLS overestimate contractility.

The claim accurately captures the need to assess all components of the mitral apparatus before measurement, the use of Carpentier's classification to differentiate primary and secondary MR, and the features making primary MR easy to identify.
The claim accurately states the definition, pathophysiology, and two main forms (atrial and ventricular) of secondary/functional mitral regurgitation.
The claim accurately states that in advanced MR or acute worsening, symptoms occur alongside left ventricular systolic dysfunction and/or pulmonary hypertension.
The claim correctly identifies myxomatous degeneration due to fibroelastic deficiency or Barlow's disease as the most common cause of primary MR in high-income countries.
The claim accurately matches the quote regarding rheumatic mitral heart disease remaining the main cause of MR in low- and middle-income countries despite decreasing prevalence.
The claim accurately describes ventricular functional MR pathophysiology (remodelling/dysfunction leading to apical tethering) and its association with ischaemic or non-ischaemic diseases.
The claim accurately describes atrial functional mitral regurgitation as the less common form characterised by annular enlargement, marked LA dilatation, and preserved LV size and function.

The claim accurately details the role of atrial fibrillation in AFMR pathogenesis, including loss of atrial kick, impaired annular mechanics, and delayed coaptation due to loss of annular size reduction.

The claim accurately reflects that chronic primary MR causes LA volume then pressure overload, requiring LVSV compensation to maintain forward stroke volume and dilating the LV via Frank-Starling mechanism.
The claim accurately describes the significance of a triangular early-peaking low-velocity continuous-wave Doppler signal in supporting severe MR and its occurrence in acute severe MR.
The claim accurately lists the components of initial assessment for MR and the clinical experience needed to identify valve-related symptoms in older patients.
The claim accurately reflects that transthoracic echocardiography is the main imaging modality for assessing mechanism, cause (etiology), severity, and repair probability in mitral regurgitation.
The claim accurately summarizes the three categories of echocardiographic parameters for grading mitral regurgitation and their respective characteristics.
The claim correctly conveys the indication for CMR and TEE when TTE is suboptimal/inconclusive, and highlights TEE's advantages in anatomical/mechanism assessment when planning surgery.
The claim states that quantifying severity is a separate assessment, whereas the quote specifies that exercise TTE is used for clinical/hemodynamic tolerance rather than to help quantify MR severity.
The claim matches the guideline quote regarding how heart valve disease affects people differently and the scope of lifestyle advice.
The claim accurately states that symptomatic or severe heart valve disease may require diuretics to reduce fluid build-up in the body and lungs.
The claim correctly details surgical options (repair vs replacement) for severe heart valve disease depending on whether the valve is seriously damaged.
The claim fully aligns with the emergency guidance for severe breathing difficulty.
The claim correctly outlines GP initial actions for symptoms of heart valve disease.
The claim accurately states the prognostic value of the new cardiac damage staging classification in asymptomatic moderate/severe primary MR.
The claim matches the advice regarding heart valve disease before or during pregnancy.
The claim accurately presents the findings from the MIDA-Quantitative registry regarding post-operative survival factors in degenerative MR.
The claim accurately reflects the guideline quote regarding how widespread availability of echocardiography identified undiagnosed RHD and demonstrated the persistent and disparate global burden.
